problem_summary.summary: Reorder nodes so values below x come before values at least x, preserving relative order within both groups.
problem_summary.input_output: Inputs: possibly-null ListNode head and integer x. Return the rearranged ListNode head. The judge supplies ListNode { int val; ListNode next; }.

brute_force.explanation: Store node references in two arrays according to the comparison with x, then reconnect the less-than group followed by the other group.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Appending during a single left-to-right scan preserves each category's original order. Concatenating the arrays places every smaller node before every remaining node.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n) — one classification pass and one relinking pass.

optimized.explanation: Build two temporary chains using dummy heads: one for values below x and one for values at least x. Terminate the second chain, then append it to the first.
optimized.correctness_idea: Each visited node is appended to exactly one chain in original scan order, preserving stability. Joining the chains enforces the partition boundary without allocating nodes.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) — each node is detached and appended once.
optimized.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary, excluding two dummy nodes and reusing input nodes.

steps.condition: 1 and 2 are below x; 3 is not.
steps.action: Append each to its category while preserving scan order.

steps.event: Append the remaining node and join the chains.
steps.action: Other chain becomes [4,3,5]; attach it after [1,2].

edge_cases.case: All nodes are below x or none are below x
edge_cases.handling: One chain remains empty and joining returns the other chain unchanged.
They belong to the at-least-x chain.
Both chains are empty and null is returned.
